relevance_note: A case report of one girl with an individual-level description and a TNFAIP3 variant: 'It revealed a nonsense mutation in the tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-induced protein 3 gene, leading to the diagnosis of haploinsufficiency A20 (HA20) (Fig. 1).'
method_note: Read only the paper, the schema, the rules and the instructions. Two in-scope people: the patient (the paper calls her 'the proband'/'our patient', role words, so label 'patient') and her father, a relative described in the text (label 'father of patient'). No table has patients as rows or columns: Table 1 is a time-course table whose columns are 'On admission', 'On hospital day 2' and 'After 9 months', so there are no ' / ' stacked cells and nothing was assigned by position; its empty cells are treated as not reported. Spans were copied by hand and re-checked against the Markdown. Uncertainties: (1) the authors state no number of patients for this report, so n_patients_reported=1 is the count of the single patient with a TNFAIP3 variant described here, and cohort_size_as_stated is null (the sentence about 'only 2 patients, including our case, have been diagnosed with HA20 in Korea [8]' is about Korea, not this study); (2) no TNFAIP3 variant is tied to the father, so he has no variants row; the only testing statement about the parents is 'We recommended NGS for her parents and younger sister, but her parents refused.', recorded in the patient's parental_testing_statement; (3) checklist item 'arthritis or arthralgia' is not reported for the father although 'arthritis' is excluded for him, and 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' is not reported for the patient although 'no uveitis was observed', because a narrower absence never excludes a broader composite item; (4) the anal ulcer is recorded as 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation'; (5) vital status, consanguinity, zygosity and inheritance are nowhere stated, so they are not reported, and vital status is left not reported even though treatment is still being considered; (6) age is printed only as 'A 9-year-old girl' at presentation, so age_at_last_evaluation_original_text is '9-year-old' and no age at diagnosis is recorded; (7) the variant is printed as 'c.547C>T' with protein 'p.Arg183^*' and the Fig. 1 legend adds 'nonsense mutation at Arg-183' (the same legend prints the typos 'TNFIP3' and 'C➞ T', kept as printed); (8) the sentence 'the TNFAIP3 (c.547C>T, p.Arg183^*) gene mutation is already known to cause HA20 [4,6,7]' names this person and this exact variant and is recorded as the authors' pathogenicity statement; (9) is_proband=false for the father and cites_prior_report_of_same_patients=false have no supporting quote, so their span is null; (10) the review counts of 89 HA20 patients [4] and of 26 studies [5] are group-level statements with no individual detail, so they yield no rows and no in-scope persons, and Table 1's per-time-point cells were not used as patient-level evidence beyond the text statements.

span: Initially, the fever recurred every 1 or 2 months; however, after tonsillectomy at 5 years of age, it recurred every 3 or 4 months.
Colchicine was started, and 9 months after treatment, oral and genital ulcers disappeared. However, the fever continued to recur every 3 or 4 months.
Currently, we are considering treatments with immune suppressants such as steroids and biologics.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: genetic testing: NGS for genes related to periodic fever and autoinflammatory syndromes revealed a nonsense mutation in TNFAIP3, leading to the diagnosis of HA20; Kikuchi disease was suggested by axillary lymph node biopsy and PFAPA syndrome was suspected clinically
span: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) for genes related to periodic fever and autoinflammatory syndromes was conducted to identify a possible genetic disorder. It revealed a nonsense mutation in the tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-induced protein 3 gene, leading to the diagnosis of haploinsufficiency A20 (HA20) (Fig. 1).
Axillary lymph node biopsy was performed, which demonstrated necrotizing lymphadenitis suggestive of Kikuchi disease.

Initially, we suspected Kikuchi disease with periodic fever, aphthous stomatitis, pharyngitis, and cervical adenitis (PFAPA) syndrome because, during the current episode, the fever had lasted for 10 days accompanied by tender lymphadenopathy.
